articleTitle: On purity theorems for vector bundles
abstract: We give criteria for vector bundles on certain complements of divisors to be trivial, in algebraic or analytic geometry.

articleTitle: Operator-valued distributions. I. Characterizations of freeness
abstract: Let M be a B-probability space. Assume that B itself is a D-probability space; then M can be viewed as D-probability space as well. Let X ∈ M. We look at the question of relating the properties of X as B-valued random variable to its properties as D-valued random variable. We characterize freeness of X from B with amalgamation over D: (a) in terms of a certain factorization condition linking the B-valued and D-valued cumulants of X, and (b) for D finite-dimensional, in terms of linking the B-valued and the D-valued Fisher information of X. We give an application to random matrices. For the second characterization, we derive a new operator-valued description of the conjugate variable and introduce an operator-valued version of the liberation gradient.

articleTitle: A new matrix-tree theorem
abstract: The classical matrix-tree theorem allows us to list the spanning trees of a graph by monomials in the expansion of the determinant of a certain matrix. We prove that in the case of three-graphs (i.e., hypergraphs whose edges have exactly three vertices), the spanning trees are generated by the Pfaffian of a suitably defined matrix. This result can be interpreted topologically as an expression for the lowest order term of the Alexander-Conway polynomial of an algebraically split link. We also prove some algebraic properties of our Pfaffian-tree polynomial.

articleTitle: The Cauchy problem for wave maps
abstract: We show global existence and uniqueness for the Cauchy problem for wave maps from the (m+1)-dimensional Minkowski space, m ≥ 4, to any complete Riemannian manifold with bounded curvature, provided the initial data are small in the critical norm.

articleTitle: Hyperelliptic Curves in Characteristic 2
On Helffer-Sjöstrand's theory of resonances
abstract: We construct a simplified version of the microlocal theory of resonances given by Helffer and Sjöstrand in (1986). This new version is based on elementary microlocal exponential estimates, and permits to recover their main results without the use of their special pseudodifferential calculus and Fourier-integral operators.

articleTitle: Cohomological localization for manifolds with boundary
abstract: For an S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>-manifold with boundary, we prove a localization formula applying to a large class of equivariant cohomology theories. We show how the localization result of Kalkman and a case of the quantization commutes with reduction theorem follow easily from the localization formula. We also derive a similar formula for actions of SU(2).

articleTitle: Extended deformation functors
abstract: We introduce a precise notion, in terms of some Schlessinger-type conditions, of extended deformation functors which is compatible with most of recent ideas in the Derived Deformation Theory (DDT) program and with geometric examples. With this notion we develop the (extended) analogue of Schlessinger and obstruction theories. The inverse mapping theorem holds for natural transformations of extended deformation functors and all such functors with finite dimensional tangent space are prorepresentable in the homotopy category. Finally we prove that the primary obstruction map induces a structure of graded Lie algebra on the tangent space.

articleTitle: On the low regularity of the Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation
abstract: We consider the Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> +u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xxx</inf> − u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">xx</inf> + uu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> = 0. We prove sharp results on the associated Cauchy problem in the Sobolev spaces H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</sup>(ℝ). For s > −1 we prove the global well-posedness of this Cauchy problem, while for s < −1 we show some ill-posedness issues. Our results hold also in the periodic case.

articleTitle: Nonfine moduli spaces of sheaves on K3 surface
abstract: In general, if M is a moduli space of stable sheaves on X, there is a unique element α in the Brauer group of M such that a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pi_M^\ast\text{?}\alpha^{-1}$</tex> -twisted universal sheaf exists on X × M. In this paper, we study the situation when X and M are K3 surfaces, and we identify α in terms of Mukai's map between the cohomology of X and of M (defined by means of a quasi-universal sheaf). We prove that the derived category of sheaves on X and the derived category of α-twisted sheaves on M are equivalent. This suggests a conjecture which describes, in terms of Hodge isometries of lattices, when derived categories of twisted sheaves on two K3 surfaces are equivalent. If proven true, this conjecture would generalize a theorem of Orlov and a recent result of Donagi-Pantev.

articleTitle: Irreducible Tori in semisimple groups (Erratum)
On the dimension of the space of cusp forms associated to 2-dimensional complex Galois representations
abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the “amplification technique” to obtain upper bounds on the dimension of spaces of automorphic forms associated to Galois representations. These bounds improve nontrivially the work of Duke (1995) on bounding the dimension of the space of weight 1 holomorphic forms.

articleTitle: Characterization of isomorphic group-subgroup subfactors
abstract: We give a necessary and sufficient condition for two inclusions of finite groups to give rise to isomorphic subfactors via the crossed product construction.

articleTitle: On totally real isotopy classes
abstract: Given two totally real embeddings j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>,j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>:M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> → ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is it possible to find an isotopy joining j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> and such that j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">t</inf> is totally real for every t? A positive answer obviously implies that j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> and j<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> belong to the same arcwise connected component of the space I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf> = I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf>(M<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>,C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup>) of totally real immersions and of the space E of ordinary embeddings. Let E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf> = I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf> ∩ E be the space of totally real embeddings and ε ∈ π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(E), i ∈ π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf>). In what follows we give an upper bound to the cardinality of π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf> ∩ ε ∩ i). In some cases—for instance if the dimension n is 3 modulo 4 - this upper bound is one and so we deduce the computation of π<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TR</inf>).

articleTitle: Hall invariants, homology of subgroups, and characteristic varieties
abstract: Given a finitely-generated group G, and a finite group Γ, Philip Hall defined δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>(G) to be the number of factor groups of G that are isomorphic to Γ. We show how to compute the Hall invariants by cohomological and combinatorial methods, when G is finitely-presented, and Γ belongs to a certain class of metabelian groups. Key to this approach is the stratification of the character variety, Hom(G,K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">*</sup>), by the jumping loci of the cohomology of G, with coefficients in rank 1 local systems over a suitably chosen field K. Counting relevant torsion points on these “characteristic” subvarieties gives δ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Γ</inf>(G). In the process, we compute the distribution of prime-index, normal subgroups K ◃ G according to dim<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">K</inf>H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(K;K), provided char K ≠ |G : K|. In turn, we use this distribution to count low-index subgroups of G. We illustrate these techniques in the case when G is the fundamental group of the complement of an arrangement of either affine lines in ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, or transverse planes in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>.

articleTitle: Reduction of structure group of principal bundles over aprojective manifold with Picard number one
abstract: Let X be a complex projective manifold with Pic(X) ≅ ℤ. Let G be a connected reductive algebraic group. A principal G-bundle will becalled split if it admits a reductionof structure group to a maximal torus of G. This corresponds tothe usual definition of a split vector bundle as a direct sum ofline bundles. Let E be a principal G-bundle on X, and let ρ : G → G′ be an injective homomorphism. We prove that if the associated principal G′-bundle E(G′) is split, then E admits a reduction to a Borel subgroupof G. Furthermore, if we assume that X is Fano or has trivialcanonical bundle, then E is also split. We apply this to obtain generalizations for principal bundles of two results about vector bundles on projective spaces. Namely, a principal G-bundle on ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is split if its restriction to a plane ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ⊂ ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is split. Also, a principal G-bundle E on ℂℙ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</sup> is trivial if there is a point p such that the restriction of E to every line through p is trivial.

articleTitle: Generating functions for intersection numbers on moduli spaces of curves
abstract: Using the connection between intersection theory on the Deligne-Mumford spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\overline{\mathcal{M}}}_{g,n}$</tex> and the edge scaling of the GUE matrix model, we express the n-point functions for the intersection numbers as n-dimensional error-function-type integrals and also give a derivation of Witten's KdV equations using the higher Fay identities of Adler, Shiota, and van Moerbeke.

articleTitle: Presenting Schur algebras
abstract: Motivated by the work of R. M. Green (1995), we obtain a presentation of Schur algebras (both the classical and quantized versions) in terms of generators and relations. The presentation is compatible with the usual presentation of the (quantized or classical) enveloping algebra of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g\ell_n$</tex> . As a result, we obtain a new integral basis for Schur algebras which is a subset of Kostant's basis of the integral form of the enveloping algebra (or its q-analogue). Projection onto an appropriate component gives a new integral basis and a presentation for the Hecke algebra, compatible with the basis and presentation for the Schur algebra. Finally, we find a second presentation of Schur algebras which is similar to Luzstig's modified form of the quantized enveloping algebra.

articleTitle: Conformal Schwarzian derivatives and conformally invariant quantization
abstract: Let (M,g) be a pseudo-Riemannian manifold. We propose a new approach for defining the conformal Schwarzian derivatives. These derivatives are 1-cocycles on the group of diffeomorphisms of M related to the modules of linear differential operators. As operators, these derivatives do not depend on the rescaling of the metric g. In particular, if the manifold (M,g) is conformally flat, these derivatives vanish on the conformal group O(p+1,q+1), where dim (M)=p+q. This work is a continuation of our previous work where the Schwarzian derivative was defined on a manifold endowed with a projective connection.

articleTitle: On the topology of compact Stein surfaces
abstract: The main result of this paper is that any compact Stein surface with boundary embeds naturally into a symplectic Lefschetz fibration over S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Also along the way we obtain the following results. (1) There exists a minimal elliptic fibration over D<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, which is not Stein. (2) The circle bundle over a genus n ≥ 2 surface with Euler number e = −1 admits at least n + 1 mutually nonhomeomorphic simply-connected Stein fillings. (3) Any surface bundle over S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, whose fiber is a closed surface of genus n ≥ 1 can be embedded into a closed symplectic 4-manifold, splittingthe symplectic 4-manifoldinto two pieces both of which have positive <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$b_2^+$</tex> . (4) Every closed, oriented, connected 3-manifold has a weakly symplectically fillable double cover, branched along a 2-component link.

articleTitle: Random Delaunay triangulations and metric uniformization
abstract: We present a new connection between the discrete conformal geometry problem of disk pattern construction and the continuous conformal geometry problem of metric uniformization. In a nutshell, we discuss how to construct disk patterns by optimizing an objective function, which turns out to be intimately related to hyperbolic volume. With the use of random Delaunay triangulations, we then average this objective function to construct an objective function on the metrics conformal to a fixed one. Finally, using this averaged objective function, we may reprove the uniformization theorem in two dimensions.

articleTitle: Todd classes of affine cones of grassmannians
abstract: A ring A, which is a homomorphic image of a regular local ring S, is said to be a Roberts ring if τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A/S</inf>([A]) = [Spec A]<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">dim A</inf>, where τ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">A/S</inf> is the Riemann-Roch map for SpecA Such rings satisfy a vanishing theorem for intersection multiplicities, as was proved by Paul Roberts in 1985. It is known that complete intersections are Roberts rings, and the first author showed that a determinantal ring is a Roberts ring precisely if it is a complete intersection. Let A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(n) denote the affine cone of the Grassmann variety G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(n) under the Plücker embedding. In this paper, we determine precisely when A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">d</inf>(n) is a Roberts ring.

articleTitle: The initial value problem for Schrödinger equations on the torus
abstract: We discuss well-posedness for the initial-boundary value problem for linear and nonlinear Schrödinger equations with periodic boundary condition. We, first, show that the initial value problem for linear equationsis L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>-well-posed if and only if the imaginary part of magnetic field has a scalar potential. Secondly, we present local existence theorem for nonlinear equations under a certain condition corresponding to that for linear equations. Lastly, we give examples of ill-posed initial value problem for nonlinear equations which do not satisfy this condition.

articleTitle: Painlevé expressions for LOE, LSE, and interpolating ensembles
abstract: We consider an ensemble which interpolates the Laguerre orthogonal ensemble (LOE) and the Laguerre symplectic ensemble (LSE). This interpolating ensemble was introduced earlier in 2001 by the author and Rains in connection with a last passage percolation model with a symmetry condition. In this paper, we obtain a Painlevé V expression for the distribution of the rightmost particle of the interpolating ensemble. Special cases of this result yield the Painlevé V expressions for the largest eigenvalues of Laguerre orthogonal ensemble and Laguerre symplectic ensemble of finite size.

articleTitle: Differential operators on the loop group via chiral algebras
abstract: Let G be an algebraic group and let <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\tilde{\mathbf g}$</tex> be the corresponding affine algebra, i.e., a central extension of the loop algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{g}{({(t)})}$</tex> corresponding to some symmetric invariant form <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q:g\otimes g\rightarrow \mathbb{C}$</tex>.Consider the induced module <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V:=\text{Ind}_{g{\lbrack{\lbrack t\rbrack}\rbrack}{(O_{G{\lbrack{\lbrack t\rbrack}\rbrack}})}}^{\widetilde g}$</tex>, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$O_{G{\lbrack{\lbrack t\rbrack}\rbrack}}$</tex> is the ring of regular functions on the group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G{\lbrack{\lbrack t\rbrack}\rbrack}$</tex>. In this paper we show that V is naturally a vertex operator algebra, which is “responsible” for D-modules on the loop group <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$G{({(t)})}$</tex>.The main technical point of the paper is that V is in fact a bimodule over the affine algebra, which we show using the techniques of VOA. This allows to prove several remarkable properties of V, one of them being the behaviour of its BRST reduction with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$g{({(t)})}$</tex>.The paper has a considerable intersection with a recent work of Gorbunov, Malikov, and Schechtman.

articleTitle: Classification of solutions of a Toda system in ℝ2
abstract: We consider solutions of the following (open) Toda system (Toda lattice) for SU(N + 1)<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-\frac12\Delta u_i=\sum_{j=1}^Na_{ij}\text{?}e^{u_j}\text{???in?}\mathbb{R}^2\qquad(1.1)$</tex>, for i = 1, 2, …, where <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K=(a_{ij})_{N\times N}$</tex> is the Cartan matrix for SU(N + 1). We show that any solution u = (u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>,…,u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf>) with<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}e^{u_i}<\infty,\text{??????}i=1,2,{\cdots},N$</tex>, can be obtained from a rational curve in ℂP<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</sup>.

articleTitle: Multi-parameter deformations of the module of symbols ofdifferential operators
abstract: The space of symbols of differential operators on a smooth manifold (i.e., the space of symmetric contravariant tensor fields) is naturally a module over the Lie algebra of vector fields. We study, in the case of ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sup> with v ≥ 2, the multi-parameter formal deformations of this module. The space of linear differential operators on ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</sup> provides an important classof such formal deformations; we show, however, that the whole space of deformations is much larger.

articleTitle: The geometry of the classical solutions of the Garnier systems
abstract: Our aim is to find a general approach to the theory of classical solutions of the Garnier system in n-variables, G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>, based on the Riemann-Hilbert problem and on the geometry of the space of isomonodromy deformations. Our approach consists in determining the monodromy data of the corresponding Fuchsian system that guarantee to have a classical solution of the Garnier system G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. This leads to the idea of the reductions of the Garnier systems. We prove that if a solution of the Garnier system G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf> is such that the associated Fuchsian system has l monodromy matrices equal to ±1, then it can be reduced classically to a solution of a the Garnier system with n − 1 variables G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n − 1</inf>. When n monodromy matrices are equal to ±1, we have classical solutions of G<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>. We give also another mechanism to produce classical solutions: we show that the solutions of the Garnier systems having reducible monodromy groups can be reduced to the classical solutions found by Okamoto and Kimura in terms of Lauricella hypergeometric functions. In the case of the Garnier system in 1-variables, i.e. for the PainlevéVI equation, we prove that all classical non-algebraic solutions have either reducible monodromy groups or at least onemonodromy matrix equal to ±1.

articleTitle: Cyclomorphy
abstract: A main result is that, roughly, a dense set of the infinitesimal trace-preserving deformations of a semicircular system σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf> arise from one-parametergroups of automorphisms of the free-group factor L(F(n)) generated by σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, …, σ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">v</inf>. More generally the paper studies cyclic gradients in von Neumann algebras, Lie algebras of noncommutative trace-preserving vector fields, and the class of cyclomorphic maps which preserve the orthogonals of spaces of cyclic gradients.

articleTitle: Siegel differential modular forms
abstract: The quotient of the moduli space of principally polarized Abelian varieties by the isogeny equivalence relation is not an object of algebraic geometry. This paper shows how this quotient space becomes a geometric object in a more general geometry (1995) obtained from “usual algebraic geometry,” by adjoining a new operation; this operation looks like a “Fermat quotient” and should be viewed as an arithmetic analogue of usual derivations.

articleTitle: Asymptotics of semiclassical soliton ensembles: rigorous justification of the WKB approximation
abstract: Rigorous pointwise asymptotics are established for semiclassical soliton ensembles (SSEs) of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation using techniques of asymptotic analysis of matrix Riemann-Hilbert problems. The accumulation of poles in the eigenfunction is handled using a new method in which the residues are simultaneously interpolated at the poles by two distinct interpolants. The results justify the WKB approximation for the nonselfadjoint Zakharov-Shabat operator with real-analytic, bell-shaped, even potentials. The new technique introduced in this paper is applicable to other problems as well: (i) it can be used to provide a unified treatment by Riemann-Hilbert methods of the zero-dispersion limit of the Korteweg-de Vries equation with negative (soliton generating) initial data as studied by Lax, Levermore, and Venakides, and (ii) it allows one to compute rigorous strong asymptotics for systems of discrete orthogonal polynomials.

articleTitle: Asymptotic properties of a family of solutionsof the Painlevé equation PVI
abstract: We study the asymptotic behavior for large argument of a family of solutions of the Painlevé equation P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">VI</inf> arising in the context of Random Matrix Theory (Borodin and Deift, 2001). We show that this family of solutions are uniquely determined by their asymptotic properties.

articleTitle: Uniform exponential growth for linear groups
abstract: This is an announcement of the theorem, with a brief sketch of the main steps in the proof, that any finitely generated group of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n</inf>(ℂ), which is not virtually solvable, has uniform exponential growth.

articleTitle: The length of the shortest closed geodesic on a 2-dimensional sphere
abstract: Let M be a Riemannian manifold homeomorphic to S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. We prove that l(M), the length of the shortest closed geodesic on M,does not exceed 4d, where d denotes the diameter of M. We also prove that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$l{(M)}\leq8\sqrt A$</tex> , where A is the area of M. These results improve the previously known inequalities by Croke (1988) and Maeda (1994).

articleTitle: Reverse bubbling and nonuniqueness in the harmonic map flow
abstract: We construct a new type of singularity which may occur inweak solutions of the harmonic map flow for two-dimensionaldomains. This “reverse bubbling” singularity may occur spontaneously, and enables us to construct solutions to theharmonic map heat equation which differ from the standardStruwe solution, despite agreeing for an arbitrarily long initialtime interval.

articleTitle: Semi-classical estimates for the resolvent in nontrapping geometries
abstract: The purpose of this note is to present a very natural and simple method to prove (for nontrapping geometries) the existence of resonance-free regions and to give estimates for the resolvent in these regions. The method is valid in any dimensions of space and does not rely on Lax and Phillips theory.

articleTitle: Formulas of Ramanujan for the power series coefficients of certain quotients of Eisenstein series
abstract: In their last joint paper, G. H. Hardy and S. Ramanujan established a formula for the power series coefficients of a broad class of nonanalytic modular forms. They then applied their theorem to 1/E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>(τ), where E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> is an Eisenstein series. In letters written to Hardy from nursing homes in England, Ramanujan communicated several other examples and further theorems on this subject. These claims have not been heretofore proved in print. Some of the examples do not fall under the purview of Hardy and Ramanujan's theorem or those of later mathematicians. The purpose of this paper is to prove several of the aforementioned results from Ramanujan's letters. To do this, extensions of the theorems of Hardy, Ramanujan, and later authors are needed.

articleTitle: Local coefficients as Mellin transforms of Bessel functions: towards a general stability
abstract: The main obstacle in extending the breakthrough in transferring generic cusp forms on odd special orthogonal groups to automorphic forms on general linear groups, recently established by the author and his collaborators, is the stability of corresponding root numbers under highly ramified twists. In this paper, the author proves a general result, expressing the reciprocals of his local coefficients for an arbitrary quasisplit group, basically as Mellin transforms of certain incomplete Bessel functions. Local root numbers are then defined inductively, using local coefficients. When combined with ideas of Cogdell and Piatetski-Shapiro on Bessel functions, this leads to a proof of stability in a number of new cases, including all the classical groups.

articleTitle: Sobolev norms of automorphic functionals
abstract: We prove a quantitative version of Frobenius reciprocity in the theory of automorphic functions. Namely, given an automorphic representation we show how to estimate the norm of the corresponding Γ-invariant functional with respect to some norms on the representation space. The answer is given by relative traces.

articleTitle: On symplectic leaves and integrable systems in standard complex semisimple Poisson-Lie groups
abstract: We provide an explicit description of symplectic leaves of a simply connected, connected, semisimple, complex Lie group equipped with the standard Poisson-Lie structure. This sharpens previously known descriptions of the symplectic leaves as connected components of certain varieties. Our main tool is the machinery of twisted generalized minors. They also allow us to present several quasi-commuting coordinate systems on every symplectic leaf. As a consequence, we construct new completely integrable systems on some special symplectic leaves.

articleTitle: Groups of connected components and congruence ideals associated with elliptic curve
abstract: Let E be a semistable elliptic curve of conductor N defined over ℚ and f be the weight-two cusp form of level N associated with E.In this paper, we consider two quantities: the order of the group of connected components of the Néron fiber of E at a prime p dividing N, and the congruence modulus, which measures congruences between f and cusp forms in the p-old subspace of the space of weight-two cusp forms of level N. We show that the l-primary part of the former divides the l-primary part of the latter if the Galois representation associated with the l-division points of E is irreducible.

articleTitle: Small representations and minuscule Richardson orbits
abstract: We study the connections between small and minuscule representations of asimple complex Lie group. We also classify the small representations in type BCFG in terms of the classification for types ADE, by means of a simple case of Langlands functorality. The main theme is the relation between small representations and unipotent classes in the dual group.

articleTitle: Hilbert schemes and W-algebras
abstract: We construct geometrically the generating fields of a W-algebra, which acts irreducibly on the direct sum of the cohomology rings of the Hilbert schemes X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[n]</sup> of n points on a projective surface X for all n ≥ 0. We compute explicitly the commutators among the Fourier components of the generating fields of the W-algebra, and identify this algebra with a W<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1+∞</inf>-type algebra. A precise formula of certain Chern character operators, which is essential for the construction of the W-algebra, is established in terms of the Heisenberg algebra generators. In addition, these Chern character operators are proved to be the zero-modes of vertex operators.

articleTitle: Motivic cohomology groups are isomorphic to higher chow groups in any characteristic
abstract: In this paper we prove that two definitions of motivic cohomologyfor smooth varieties over any field agree. The first definitionis the one used in the proof of the Milnor conjecture. The secondone was shown by Friedlander and Suslin to agree withBloch's higher Chow groups. A proof of the main theorem of thispaper was previously known for varieties over fields withresolution of singularities.

articleTitle: Integrals of Eisenstein series and derivatives of L-functions
abstract: In his lost notebook, Ramanujan recorded a formula relating a “character analogue” of the Dedekind eta-function, the integral of a quotient of eta-functions, and the value of a Dirichlet L-function at s = 2. Here, we derive an infinite family of formulas which includes Ramanujan's original formula as a special case. Our results depend on a representation of values of the derivatives of Dirichlet L-functions as the limiting values of certain q-series.

articleTitle: Spectral deformations and Eisenstein series associated with modular symbols
abstract: We give a new proof of the analytic continuation of the Eisenstein series associated with modular symbols. We study its singularities, analytic properties, and functional equation using perturbation theory of the Laplace operator on character varieties.

articleTitle: Odd dimensional tori are contact manifolds
abstract: We show that, for every contact manifold M and for every Riemann surface Σ of genus at least 1, the manifold Σ × M admits a contact structure. In particular, the tori T<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2n+1</sup> are contact manifolds.

articleTitle: Ideal classes of the Weyl algebra and noncommutative projective geometry (with an appendix by Michel Van den Bergh)
abstract: Let R be the set of isomorphism classes of right ideals in the Weyl algebra A = A<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(ℂ), and let C be the set of isomorphism classes of triples <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V;\text{X},\text{Y})$</tex> , where V is a finite-dimensional (complex) vector space, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{X},\text{Y}$</tex> are endomorphisms of V such that <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\lbrack\text{X},\text{Y}\rbrack}+\text{I}$</tex> has rank 1. Following a suggestion of L. Le Bruyn, we define a map θR → C by appropriately extending an ideal of A to a sheaf over a quantum projective plane, and then using standard methods of homological algebra. We prove that θ is inverse to a bijection ω:C → R, constructed, by the authors in 2000, by a completely different method. The main step in the proof is to show that θ is equivariant with respect to natural actions of the group G = Aut(A) on R and C: for that we have to study also the extensions of an ideal to certain weighted quantum projective planes. Along the way, we find an elementary description of θ.

articleTitle: Extensions of number fields with wild ramification of bounded depth
abstract: We consider p-extensions of number fields such that the filtration of the Galois group by higher ramification groups is of prescribed finite length. We extend well-known properties of tame extensions to this more general setting; for instance, we show that these towers, when infinite, are “asymptotically good,” (an explicit bound for the root discriminant is given). We study the difficult problem of bounding the relation-rank of the Galois groups in question. Results of Gordeev and Wingberg imply that the relation-rank can tend to infinity when the set of ramified primes is fixed but the length of the ramification filtration becomes large. We show that all p-adic representations of these Galois groups are potentially semistable; thus, a conjecture of Fontaine and Mazur on the structure of tamely ramified Galois p-extensions extends to our case. Further evidence in support of this conjecture is presented.

articleTitle: On a conjecture of Savin
abstract: We consider <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\otimes\theta^\ast$</tex> , the inner tensor product of two exceptional representations of the general linear group. It is shown that those spherical representations lying in the image of the tautological lift from an appropriate orthogonal or symplectic group occur as quotients of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\otimes\theta^\ast$</tex> . This result accords with a conjectural description of the spherical constituents of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta\otimes\theta^\ast$</tex> formulated by Savin.

articleTitle: An elliptic incarnation of the Bailey chain
abstract: For the first time a Bailey chain with all entries composed out of the Jacobi theta functions is constructed. This is an elliptic extension of the WP (well-poised) Bailey chain of Andrews and it generates an infinite sequence of identities for theta hypergeometric series. As a particular example, we obtained a new proof of the Frenkel-Turaev elliptic analogue of the Bailey transformation for a terminating <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> basic hypergeometric series. An elliptic generalization of the Andrews-Berkovich <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> → <inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</inf>Φ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> transformation formula is derived by employing an elliptic extension of a Bressoud's Bailey pair.

articleTitle: On a sharp estimate for oscillatory integrals associated with the Schrödinger equation
abstract: The problem solved here rises in a natural way from certain estimates associated with the almost everywhere convergence to the initial datum of the solution to the Schrödinger equation, assuming minimum smoothness. The result gives precise information about the uniform integrability properties of Bessel functions against the oscillatory term <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$e^{itx^2}$</tex> .

articleTitle: On families of triangular Hopf algebras
abstract: Following the ideas of our previous works, we study families of triangular Hopf algebras obtained by twisting finite supergroups by a twist lying entirely in the odd part. These families are parameterized by data (G, V, u, B), where G is a finite group, V its finite-dimensional representation, u a central element of G of order 2 acting by −1 on V, and B an element of S<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V. We fix the discrete data G, V, u, and find the set of isomorphism classes of the members of the family as Hopf algebras, in terms of the continuous parameter B. This set is often infinite, which provides examples of non-trivial continuous families of triangular Hopf algebras. The lowest dimension in which such a family occurs is 32, in which case we get 3 families which are dual to the 3 families of pointed Hopf algebras of dimension 32 constructed recently by Graña. Furthermore, we show that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(S^2V)^G=0$</tex> then such continuous families are non-trivial not only up to a Hopf algebra isomorphism, but also up to twisting of the multiplication. Thus, they provide counterexamples to Masuoka's weakened Kaplansky's 10th conjecture, which claims that up to twisting, there are finitely many types of Hopf algebras in each dimension. Finally, we study the algebra structure of the duals of our families, and show they are direct sums of Clifford algebras. Since there are finitely many types of Clifford algebras in each dimension, this allows us to construct non-trivial families of rigid tensor structures on the abelian category of modules over a finite-dimensional algebra, with a fixed Grothendieck ring.

articleTitle: Invariance principle for inverse problems
abstract: Consider the nonlinear mapping F : H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> → H given by F(y) = y″+u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(y′)+u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>(y)−u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>(y,y′), y ∈ H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, where the Hilbert spaces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$H={\{q:q\in L_{\text{?}R}^{\text{?}2}{(\text{T})},\int_{\text{?}0}^{\text{?}1}q{(x)}\text{?}dx=0\}}$</tex> and H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> = {y,y″ ∈ H}. Here, the functions u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are real analytic and u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>′(y)≤ 0; the constant u<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is such that F(y) ∈ H. We prove that the map F is a real analytic isomorphism. Furthermore, a priori 2-sided estimates of the norms of F(y), y are obtained. We apply these results to the inverse problems for the Schrödinger operators −d<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>dx<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+q(x) in L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(ℝ) with a 1-periodic potential. In particular, we use this result to study the Camassa-Holm equation.

articleTitle: A counterexample to the Hodge conjecture extended to Kähler varieties
abstract: We show that rational Hodge classes on a compact Kähler variety X are not in general generated by the Chern classes of analytic coherent sheaves on X. We also show in an appendix that analytic coherent sheaves on a compact Kähler variety X do not in general admit a finite resolution by locally free sheaves.

articleTitle: Convex decomposition theory
abstract: We use convex decomposition theory to (1) reprove the existence of a universally tight contact structure on every irreducible 3-manifold with nonempty boundary, and (2) prove that every toroidal 3-manifold carries infinitely many nonisotopic, nonisomorphic tight contact structures.

articleTitle: On convergence of moments for random Young tableaux and a random growth model
abstract: In recent work of Baik, Deift, and Rains convergence of moments was established for the limiting joint distribution of the lengths of the first k rows in random Young tableaux. The main difficulty was obtaining a good estimate for the tail of the distribution and this was accomplished through a highly nontrival Riemann-Hilbert analysis. Here we give a simpler derivation. The same method is used to establish convergence of moments for a random growth model.

articleTitle: Perturbations of one-dimensional Schrödinger operators preserving the absolutely continuous spectrum
abstract: The stability of the absolutely continuous spectrum of one-dimensional Schrödinger operators, [Hu](x) = −u″(x) + q(x)u(x), under perturbations of the potential is discussed. The focus is on demonstrating this stability under minimal assumptions on how fast the perturbation decays at infinity. We present a general technique together with sample applications. These include the following: for an operator with a periodic potential, any perturbation V ∈ L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> preserves the absolutely continuous spectrum. For the Stark operator, the same is true for pertubations with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\int\vert V(t^2)\vert^2dt<\infty$</tex> . Both of these results are known to be optimal, in the sense that the integrability index cannot be increased.

articleTitle: Embedding dimensions of Poisson spaces
abstract: We give lower bounds on the Poisson embedding dimension of asingular quotient of a symplectic manifold by doing a local calculation in formal power series. In particular, we show that the Poisson embedding dimension of the weight-(1,1,2) resonance space is at least 13.

articleTitle: Homotopy groups of complements and nonisolated singularities
abstract: We study the topology of the level sets f = t, where f = 0 has a nonisolated singularity, in two cases: f is a polynomial function on ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</sup> with one atypical value, or f is a germ of a holomorphic function. In both cases we relate certain homology groups of the relevant level sets to the homotopy groups of complements of f = 0. As a consequence, we obtain the relationship between these homology groups and the data obtained from the “position of singularities” on a hyperplane section close to the hyperplane section passing through the singularity. We also obtain new vanishing results for the homotopy groups of the complements to affine hypersurfaces in ℂ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">n+1</sup>, in terms of the behavior at infinity.

articleTitle: Uniform approximate functional equation for principal L-functions
abstract: We prove an approximate functional equation for the central valueof the L-series attached to an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation π of GL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> over a number field with unitary central character and contragradient representation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\widetilde\pi$</tex> . The approximation involves a smooth truncation of the Dirichletseries L(s,π) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L{(s,\widetilde\pi)}$</tex> after about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt C$</tex> terms, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C=C{(\pi)}=C{(\widetilde\pi)}$</tex> being the analytic conductorintroduced by Iwaniec and Sarnak (2000). We investigate the decayrate of the cutoff function and its derivatives. Wealso see that the truncation can be made uniformly explicit atthe cost of an error term. Straightforwardextensions of these results exist for products of central values. We hope that these formulae will help further understanding ofthe central values of principal L-functions, such as findinggood bounds on their various power means, or establishingsubconvexity or nonvanishing results in certain families. A crucial role in the proofs is played by recent progress on theRamanujan-Selberg conjectures achieved by Luo, Rudnick and Sarnak(1999). The bounds at the non-Archimedean places enter throughthe work of Molteni (2002). Uniform approximate functional equation for principal L-functions (erratum) dx.doi.org/10.1155/S1073792804139986

articleTitle: On Kazhdan constants and mixing of random walks
abstract: Let G be a group with Kazhdan's property (T), and let S be a transitive generating set (there exists a group H ⊂ Aut (G) which acts transitively on S). In this paper, we relate two definitions of the Kazhdan constant and the eigenvalue gap in this case. Applications to various random walks on groups and the product replacement random algorithm are also presented.

articleTitle: On the structure of embedded minimal annuli
abstract: We show that any embedded minimal annulus in a ball (with boundary in the boundary of the ball and) with a small neck can be decomposed by a simple closed geodesic into two graphical subannuli. Moreover, we give a sharp bound for the length of this closed geodesic in terms of the separation (or height) between the graphical subannuli. This will illustrate our “pair of pants” decomposition in the special case where the embedded minimal planar domain is an annulus. The catenoid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\{x_1^2+x_2^2=\text{cosh}^2x_3\}$</tex> is the prime example of an embedded minimal annulus.

articleTitle: Invariant Stein domains in Stein symmetric spaces anda nonlinear complex convexity theorem
abstract: We prove a complex version of Kostant's non-linear convexity theorem. Applications to the construction of G-invariant Grauert tubes of Riemannian symmetric spaces G/K are given.

articleTitle: Diophantine inequalities on projective varieties
abstract: We deduce a quantitative version of a Diophantine approximation result of Faltings and Wüstholz (1994) dealing with systems of Diophantine inequalities to be solved in algebraic points of a projective variety X. Our method consists of embedding X into a linear variety by means of a suitable Veronese map, and then applying a recent quantitative version of the subspace theorem due to Evertse and Schlickewei. To construct the Veronese map, we prove a result of independent interest, which gives a lower bound for the mth normalized Hilbert weight of X in terms of the normalized Chow weight of X.

articleTitle: Two types of distinguished supercuspidal representations
abstract: When π is an irreducible, tame supercuspidal representation of G = GL(n, F), for some p-adic field F, we study the space Hom<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf>(n + 1), where H is a subgroup of G of two possible types: (i) G = GL(n,F′), where F/F′ is quadratic, or (ii) G = GL(n/2,F) × GL(n/2,F). Applications to L-functions and lifting problems are discussed.

articleTitle: Semiclassical geometry of quantum line bundles and Morita equivalence of star products
abstract: We show how deformation quantization of line bundles over a Poisson manifold M produces a canonical action Φ of the Picard group Pic(M)≅ H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>(M, ℤ on the moduli space of equivalence classes of differential star products on M, Def<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">diff</inf>(M). The orbits of Φ characterize Morita equivalent star products on M. We describe the semiclassical limit of Φ in terms of the characteristic classes of star products by studying the semiclassical geometry of deformed line bundles.

articleTitle: The arithmetic of prime degree trees
abstract: The goal of this article is to relate the combinatorics of a particular kind of dessin d'enfant, namely a noncyclotomic tree T with p edges for some prime p, to the ramification behavior of p in the moduli field of T. The proof of the theorem follows from a series of lemmas describing properties of particular models for T, called normalized and canonicalmodels. As a consequence of the main theorem, we give an example in which we can show that a valency class of trees forms a single Galois orbit. This kind of result is inaccessible using only the usual theory of combinatorial Galois invariants of dessins, as these can only separate Galois orbits, but not confirm that two trees really belong to the same Galois orbit.

articleTitle: A differential ideal of symmetric polynomials spanned by Jack polynomials at rβ = -(r=1)/(k+1)
abstract: For each pair of positive integers (k,r) such that k+1, r−1 are coprime, we introduce an ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{{(k,r)}}$</tex> of the ring of symmetric polynomials <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbb{C}{\lbrack x_1,\dots,x_n\rbrack}^{S_n}$</tex> . The ideal <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{{(k,r)}}$</tex> has a basis consisting of Jack polynomials with parameter rβ=-(r−1)/(k+1), and admits an action of a family of differential operators of Dunkl type including the positive half of the Virasoro algebra. The space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{{(k,2)}}$</tex> coincides with the space of all symmetric polynomials in n variables which vanish when k+1 variables are set equal. The space <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_n^{{(2,r)}}$</tex> coincides with the space of correlation functions of an Abelian current of a vertex operator algebra related to Virasoro minimal series (3,r+2).

articleTitle: Estimates for parametric elliptic integrands
abstract: We bound area and total curvature for intrinsic balls in surfaces which are stable. An important feature is that there are no a priori assumptions on the surface. The fact that the argument applies (and gives good estimates) to more general domains than intrinsic balls plays a key role in our study (given elsewhere) of general (not necessarily stable) embedded minimal surfaces.

articleTitle: The charge conjugation orbifold $V_{\mathbb{Z}\alpha}^+$ is rational when 〈α, α〉 / 2 is prime
abstract: In this paper we prove the rationality of the vertex operator algebra <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_L^+$</tex> for a rank one positive definite even lattice L whose generator has a prime half length.

articleTitle: G-bundles, isomonodromy, and quantum Weyl groups
abstract: First an “irregular Riemann-Hilbert correspondence” is established for meromorphic connections on principal G-bundlesover a disc, where G is any connected complex reductive group. Secondly, in the case of poles of order two, isomonodromic deformations of such connections are considered and it is proved that the classical actions of quantum Weyl groups found by De Concini, Kac, and Procesi do arise from isomonodromy (and so have a purely geometrical origin). Finally, a certain flat connection appearing in the work of De Concini and Toledano Laredo is derived from isomonodromy, indicating that the above result is the classical analogue of their conjectural Kohno-Drinfeld theorem for quantum Weyl groups.

articleTitle: Relaxation of excited states in nonlinear Schrödinger equations
abstract: We consider a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a bounded local potential in ℝ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The linear Hamiltonian is assumed to have two bound states with the eigenvalues satisfying some resonance condition. Suppose that the initial data is small and is near some nonlinear excited state. We give a sufficient condition on the initial data so that the solution to the Schrödinger equation approaches to certain nonlinear ground state as the time tends to infinity. Our proof is based on a notion of outgoing estimate which measures the time-direction related information of the wave functions for the nonlinear Schrödinger equations.

articleTitle: Singular principal bundles over higher-dimensional manifolds andtheir moduli spaces
abstract: We introduce the notion of a singular principal G-bundle, associated to a reductive algebraic group G over the complex numbers by means of a faithful representation ρ′ : G → SL(V). This concept is meant to provide an analog to the notion of a torsion free sheaf as a generalization of the notion of a vector bundle. We construct moduli spaces for these singular principal bundles which compactify the moduli spaces of stable principal bundles.

articleTitle: Hexagonal circle patterns and integrable systems: patterns with the multi-ratio property and Lax equations on the regular triangular lattice
abstract: Hexagonal circle patterns are introduced, and a subclass thereof is studied in detail. It is characterized by the following property: for every circle the multi-ratio of its six intersection points with neighboring circles is equal to −1. The relation of such patterns with an integrable system on the regular triangular lattice is established. A kind of a Bäcklund transformation for circle patterns is studied. Further, a class of isomonodromic solutions of the aforementioned integrable system is introduced, including circle patterns analogs to the analytic functions z<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sup> and logz.

articleTitle: Selmer groups and Chow groups of self-products of algebraic varieties
abstract: Let X be a proper flat scheme over the ring of integers of a global field. We show that the Tate conjecture and the finiteness of the Chow group of vertical cycles on self-products of X implies the vanishing of the dual Selmer group of certain twists of tensor powers of representations occurring in the étale cohomology of X.

articleTitle: On the topology of algebraic surfaces and reduction modulo p
abstract: We show that the topology of a simply-connected smooth projective surface is determined by its algebraic structure modulo p.

articleTitle: A priori Lp-estimates for solutions of Riemann-Hilbert problems
abstract: We use steepest-descent ideas to obtain a priori L<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">p</sup>-estimates for solutions of Riemann-Hilbert problems. Such estimates play a crucial role, in particular, in analyzing the long-time behavior of solutions of the perturbed nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the line.

articleTitle: Modularity of solvable Artin representations of GO(4)-type
abstract: Let F be a number field with absolute Galois group G. We associate to each solvable representation with finite image of G of GO(4)-type, an automorphic form of GL(4)/F with the same L-function. As a consequence we exhibit an infinite class of primitive, 16-dimensional representations for which the Artin conjecture holds.

articleTitle: Quasi-invariants of Coxeter groups and m-harmonic polynomials
abstract: The space of m-harmonic polynomials related to a Coxeter group G and a multiplicity function m on its root system is defined as the joint kernel of the properly gauged invariant integrals of the corresponding generalised quantum Calogero-Moser problem. The relation between this space and the ring of all quantum integrals of this system (which is isomorphic to the ring of corresponding quasiinvariants) is investigated.

articleTitle: Quantization of Slodowy slices
abstract: We give a direct proof of (a slight generalization of) the recent result of Premet (1999) related to generalized Gelfand-Graev representations and of an equivalence due to Skryabin (2000).

articleTitle: Multivalued minimal graphs and properness of disks
abstract: The point of this paper is two-fold: first, we give new estimates for multi-valued solutions u of the minimal surface equation. Second, we apply these to prove that certain embedded minimal disks are properly embedded.

articleTitle: Estimates for nonsingular multiplicative character sums
abstract: We give estimates for “nonsingular” multiplicative character sums in several variables over finite fields which are in complete analogy with the fundamental results of Deligne for the corresponding additive character sums.

articleTitle: Generalized Hunt-Dyson formula and Bohnenblust-Spitzer theorem
abstract: Let m be a natural number, and assume that a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf> are real. Let n be an arbitrary natural power. Consider the maximum of zero and the accumulating sums a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>, a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>+a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and up to a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>+a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>+…+a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>. We prove a combinatorial identity for this maximum raised to the power n and summed over the set of all permutations of the variables a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>,…,a<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">m</inf>. We call this identity the generalized Hunt-Dyson formula (gHD). In the case of the power n=1 it reduces to the usual Hunt-Dyson formula (HD). In this paper, we derive the gHD from the renowned Bohnenblust-Spitzer combinatorial theorem (BSt). We give also a sketch of an independent proof of the gHD based on a generalization of Dyson's proof of the HD. After that we derive the BSt from the gHD providing the former with a new proof. The formula gHD is related to two problems in analysis. The first one is a computation of lower order asymptotic terms in a generalization of the strong Szegö limit theorem for a pseudodifferential operator on a Zoll manifold of any dimension, in particular for the standard sphere of any dimension. The second application of the gHD is a formula for an arbitrary order moment of the maximum of a random walk with independent identically distributed steps.

articleTitle: Semi-infinite variations of Hodge structures and integrablehierarchies of KdV type
abstract: We consider integrable KdV type hierarchy associated naturally with arbitrary semi-simple Frobenius manifolds. Equations defining hierarchy have Lax form and admit bihamiltonian description. This hierarchy is responsible for extension of corresponding semi-infinite variation of Hodge structures by generating variations along higher times {t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α,r</sup>} satisfying (∂ / ∂ t<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α,r</sup>)L(t)⊆ħ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−r</sup>L(t).

articleTitle: Integrable systems on quad-graphs
abstract: We consider general integrable systems on graphs as discrete flat connections with the values in loop groups. We argue that a certain class of graphs is of a special importance in this respect, namely quad-graphs, the cellular decompositions of oriented surfaces with all two-cells being quadrilateral. We establish a relation between integrable systems on quad-graphs and discrete systems of the Toda type on graphs. We propose a simple and general procedure for deriving discrete zero curvature representations for integrable systems on quad-graphs, based on the principle of the three-dimensional consistency. Thus, finding a zero curvature representation is put on an algorithmic basis and does not rely on the guesswork anymore. Several examples of integrable systems on quad-graphs are considered in detail, their geometric interpretation is given in terms of circle patterns.

articleTitle: Braid group actions and tensor products
abstract: We define an action of the braid group of a simple Lie algebra on the space of imaginary roots in the corresponding quantum affine algebra. We then use this action to determine an explicit condition for a tensor product of arbitrary irreducible finite-dimensional representations to be cyclic. This allows us to determine the set of points at which the corresponding R-matrix has a zero.

articleTitle: Complexes of modules over exceptional Lie superalgebras E(3,8) and E(5,10)
abstract: Complexes of generalized Verma modules over the infinite-dimensional exceptional Lie superalgebras E(3,8) and E(5,10) are constructed and studied.

articleTitle: Universality for eigenvalue correlations from the modified Jacobi unitary ensemble
abstract: The eigenvalue correlations of random matrices from the Jacobi unitary ensemble have a known asymptotic behavior as their size tends to infinity. In the bulk of the spectrum, the behavior is described in terms of the sine kernel, and at the edge in terms of the Bessel kernel. We prove that this behavior persists for the modified Jacobi unitary ensemble. This generalization of the Jacobi unitary ensemble is associated with the modified Jacobi weight w(x) = (1−x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">α</sup> (1+x)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rβ</sup> h(x) where the extra factor h is assumed to be real analytic and strictly positive on [−1,1]. We use the connection with the orthogonal polynomials with respect to the modified Jacobi weight, and recent results on strong asymptotics derived by McLaughlin, Van Assche, and the authors of this paper.
